description:
This role is for one of our clients 
 Compensation: $150 per hour 
 
 Role Type: Contract
 Work Commitment: 30–40 hours per week
 Work Arrangement: Remote, Flexible Schedule
 Role Overview
 Join a leading AI research team's Generative AI (GenAI) initiative and contribute to the development of foundational AI models. We are looking for experienced Software Engineers who are established open-source maintainers or core contributors with substantial hands-on ownership of mature, widely adopted open-source codebases.
 In this role, you will leverage your practical engineering expertise, repository knowledge, and senior-level code review judgment to help improve AI systems' capabilities in software engineering, code quality, and open-source maintenance. You will work closely with AI researchers and engineering teams to create realistic coding challenges, develop reference solutions, evaluate AI-generated code, and provide high-quality technical feedback.
 The engagement requires a commitment of 30–40 hours per week, with flexible scheduling. Most tasks are asynchronous and can be completed during evenings or weekends, with occasional meetings with research teams as required.
 Requirements 
 Key Responsibilities
 Collaborate with AI research and engineering teams to identify knowledge gaps and improve model performance in software engineering, code review, debugging, and open-source project maintenance.
 Develop challenging, realistic engineering tasks based on an open-source repository you actively maintain or contribute to. Tasks may include feature development, code refactoring, bug fixes, testing, and other responsibilities typically handled by experienced maintainers.
 Create accurate, well-structured reference implementations and solutions that demonstrate strong engineering practices and repository-specific conventions.
 Review and evaluate AI-generated code, test cases, and grading rubrics against the project's architecture, coding standards, maintainability requirements, and quality benchmarks.
 Build, configure, and execute the open-source project locally, including using Docker, to validate tasks, reference solutions, and test suites.
 Assess code quality, identify edge cases, detect potential bugs, and evaluate the correctness, reliability, and maintainability of AI-generated changes.
 Write detailed technical explanations and rationales outlining expected solution quality, identifying shortcomings, and explaining important engineering decisions.
 Provide actionable written feedback to help improve AI-generated code and strengthen model performance.
 Work with other subject matter experts to maintain consistency, technical accuracy, and quality across AI training datasets.
 Required Skills and Qualifications
 Established Open-Source Experience: Must be a recognised maintainer or core contributor to a widely used open-source software project.
 Maintainer Criteria: Listed in the repository's MAINTAINERS or CODEOWNERS file, or have completed at least 10 pull request (PR) reviews within the last 12 months.
 Core Contributor Criteria: Have at least 3 substantive merged pull requests within the last 12 months.
 Repository Maturity: The project must be at least two years old, have an established user base, maintain an active code review culture, and consist primarily of human-written code.
 Verifiable Contribution History: Demonstrated history of sustained open-source contributions, publicly verifiable through the candidate's own GitHub account.
 Advanced Code Review Expertise: Strong engineering judgment and the ability to critically assess AI-generated code, test coverage, edge cases, architecture, and implementation quality.
 Hands-on Development Skills: Ability to independently build, configure, run, and test the project and its test suite locally, including through Docker.
 Technical Communication: Excellent written communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts, code review decisions, and engineering trade-offs clearly.
 Independent Ownership: Ability to develop tasks, validate solutions, and provide technical feedback independently, ensuring all written rationales and evaluations are personally authored.
 Engagement Requirements
 Availability to commit 30–40 hours per week as the primary professional focus. This engagement is not suitable for individuals simultaneously holding another full-time job.
 Exclusivity throughout the engagement, with no concurrent work for another AI research lab or AI training organisation, including other similar project engagements.
 Must be legally authorised to work in the country of residence.
 Willingness to complete required background verification and sign confidentiality agreements before commencing work.
 Ability to work using a company-provided device to maintain information security and confidentiality.
 Availability for occasional discussions and meetings with AI researchers and engineering teams as required.
